hunks.baseline: My ears went numb beneath the deafening crash.
hunks.sol: The deafening crash left my ears numb.

hunks.baseline: It felt as if a giant’s palm had smacked my entire body.
hunks.sol: It felt as if a giant’s palm had struck my entire body.

hunks.baseline: The irresistible force sent me flying backward. I twisted in midair, and a blade of gray energy came rushing toward my face.
hunks.sol: The force sent me flying backward. The moment I twisted in midair, a blade of gray energy came rushing toward my face.

hunks.baseline: I snapped my head aside, and the gray energy skimmed past the tip of my nose, cleaving the ground like soft tofu. I landed lightly on the spot it had cut through.
hunks.sol: I snapped my head aside. The gray energy skimmed the tip of my nose and sliced through the ground like soft tofu. I landed lightly above the cut.

hunks.baseline: Then I watched one man walk toward me, his entire body wrapped in gray energy.
hunks.sol: Then I watched a man walk toward me, his entire body wrapped in gray energy.

hunks.baseline: He smiled at the sound of my voice. The shadow in his deep-set dimples seemed especially dark. That wasn’t just my imagination.
hunks.sol: He smiled at the sound of my voice. The shadow in his deep-set dimple seemed especially dark. That wasn’t just my imagination.

hunks.baseline: The energy pouring from Michael Silbert was so overwhelming that even those fighting nearby choked on their breath and retreated as far as they could.
hunks.sol: The energy pouring from Michael Silbert was so overwhelming that even those fighting nearby caught their breath and put as much distance between themselves and him as they could.

hunks.baseline: I couldn’t back down. And I had no intention of doing so.
hunks.sol: I couldn’t back down. I had no intention of doing so.

hunks.baseline: Just as I’d decided before coming here, all I could do was fight back.
hunks.sol: Just as I’d decided before coming here, I would fight.

hunks.baseline: To stop that leisurely approaching monster. To keep him from hurling billions of people into the flames all over again.
hunks.sol: To stop that monster strolling toward me. To keep him from hurling billions of people into the flames all over again.

hunks.baseline: I stepped forward, putting my weight into it.
hunks.sol: I stepped forward with all my strength.

hunks.baseline: The wind brushed past my body, and space folded. At the same time, two keywords completed themselves in my mind and became commands.
hunks.sol: Wind brushed past my body, and space folded. At the same time, two keywords formed in my mind and became commands.

hunks.baseline: A spear I’d hidden where no one could see it wrapped itself in my hand.
hunks.sol: The spear I’d hidden where no one could see it settled into my grip.

hunks.baseline: The world had slowed. Blue-white flames surged up along the spearhead, painting the gray eyes where darkness rippled as I brought it down.
hunks.sol: The world had slowed. Blue-white flames surged along the spearhead, painting the gray eyes where darkness rippled as I brought it down.

hunks.baseline: Every trace of moisture within several meters evaporated beneath the concentrated heat.
hunks.sol: The concentrated heat evaporated every trace of moisture within several meters.

hunks.baseline: Through air hot enough to catch fire at a touch, I saw his eyes fly wide.
hunks.sol: Through air hot enough to catch fire at a touch, I saw his eyes widen.

hunks.baseline: And the corners of his mouth were still turned up, even in the face of an attack no one here could have expected.
hunks.sol: The corners of his mouth were still turned up, even in the face of a strike no one here could have expected.

hunks.baseline: A sword shot upward like a streak of light and smashed into the White Flame spearhead falling toward his crown.
hunks.sol: A sword flashed upward like a streak of light and struck the spearhead of White Flame as it fell toward his crown.

hunks.baseline: “So that’s it. I wondered why I’d never seen that spear.”
hunks.sol: “So that’s it. I’d been wondering why I never saw that spear.”

hunks.baseline: “So, are you done with the surprise magic trick you prepared?”
hunks.sol: “Are you done with the surprise magic trick you prepared?”

hunks.baseline: A strength impossible to believe belonged to a human, and an unprecedented power that seemed to well up without end, burst forth all at once.
hunks.sol: Strength no human should have possessed and a boundless, unprecedented power burst forth all at once.

hunks.baseline: The moment I faced that immense power head-on, I realized with absolute certainty:
hunks.sol: The moment I faced that immense force head-on, I knew for certain:

hunks.baseline: Even the physical abilities I’d pushed far beyond their limits thanks to the System, even my three jiazi of internal energy—a level no one in Murim could afford to underestimate—weren’t enough to fully suppress him.
hunks.sol: Even my physical abilities, pushed far beyond their limits thanks to the System, and my three jiazi of internal energy—a level no one in Murim could afford to underestimate—weren’t enough to fully suppress his power.

hunks.baseline: *If the fallout from this power reaches the people around us…*
hunks.sol: *If the fallout reaches the people around us…*

hunks.baseline: At least dozens would die. And half of them would be heroes who shouldn’t die here.
hunks.sol: At least dozens would die. Half of them would be heroes who should never die in a place like this.

hunks.baseline: In the end, I had only one option left.
hunks.sol: I had only one option left.

hunks.baseline: With that word flashing through my mind, I let go of the White Flame, which had been flung upward by the force of the clash, and threw out both hands without hesitation.
hunks.sol: With that word flashing through my mind, I let go of White Flame, flung upward by the force of the clash, and thrust out both hands without hesitation.

hunks.baseline: Two branches from the same root—the Fire Gate Clan—sent two streams of flame surging into the murky aura.
hunks.sol: Two branches from the same root—the Fire Gate Clan. From their tips, two streams of flame surged into the murky aura.

hunks.baseline: The tremendous recoil sent throbbing pain through my body. The ground turned over beneath my sliding toes, revealing its ugly innards in long furrows.
hunks.sol: The tremendous recoil sent throbbing pain through my body. The ground turned over beneath my sliding feet, exposing its ugly innards in long furrows.

hunks.baseline: But I focused only on the energy in front of me. I kept pouring the flames from both hands into the murky aura.
hunks.sol: But I focused only on the energy in front of me, pouring the flames from both hands into the murky aura.

hunks.baseline: Not stopping it—throwing it out of balance.
hunks.sol: Not stopping it—breaking it apart.

hunks.baseline: At last, the mass of destructive energy had visibly shrunk. I twisted it with all my strength and hurled it behind me.
hunks.sol: At last, the mass of destructive energy visibly shrank. I twisted it with all my strength and hurled it behind me.

hunks.baseline: The Skeleton King had just plunged his Bone Sword into the chest of one of the traitors, who’d staggered off balance. He shouted,
hunks.sol: The Skeleton King drove his Bone Sword into the chest of a traitor who had staggered off balance, then shouted, “Watch out!”

hunks.baseline: “Watch out!”
I dodged his lightning-fast thrust and closed in, driving my fist at him without hesitation.
hunks.sol: I dodged the lightning-fast thrust and slipped inside his reach, driving a fist at him without hesitation.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert blocked my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist with a hand wrapped in layer upon layer of aura, then raised his knee.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert blocked my Flame-Extinguishing Divine Fist with a hand wrapped in layer upon layer of aura, then brought his knee up.

hunks.baseline: No—he was about to raise it, but suddenly shoved me away and retreated.
hunks.sol: No—just as he was about to, he shoved me away and retreated.

hunks.baseline: A silver streak plunged viciously from the air, piercing exactly the spot where he’d stood a moment ago.
hunks.sol: A silver streak plunged from the air, piercing the exact spot where he’d stood a moment ago.

hunks.baseline: Watching me silently draw the White Flame, he smiled softly.
hunks.sol: He watched me silently pull White Flame free, then smiled.

hunks.baseline: I looked around at the screams and blood splashing everywhere. A bitter laugh escaped me before I knew it.
hunks.sol: I looked around at the screams and the blood spraying everywhere. A disbelieving laugh escaped me.

hunks.baseline: “I’ve experienced imbalances like this several times before. The stronger my magical power grew, the more it fell out of balance with my mana. There were even times I couldn’t control the magical power I absorbed from Magic Gems. But do you know what I thought of every time that happened?”
hunks.sol: “I’ve experienced imbalances like this several times before. The stronger my magical power grew, the further it fell out of balance with my mana. There were even times I couldn’t control the magical power I absorbed from Magic Gems. But do you know what I thought every time it happened?”

hunks.baseline: Hundreds of Hunters were fighting a horrific civil war in the same room, but his expression was utterly at ease as he watched.
hunks.sol: Hundreds of Hunters were fighting a horrific civil war in the same room, but he looked utterly at ease as he watched.

hunks.baseline: “If someone kept getting in my way. If I couldn’t reach the pinnacle as a human because of them… I thought it wouldn’t be so bad to succeed Asmodeus as the new Demon King.”
hunks.sol: “If someone kept getting in my way. If they prevented me from reaching the pinnacle as a human… I thought becoming the new Demon King after Asmodeus wouldn’t be so bad.”

hunks.baseline: I stared at Michael Silbert, at a loss for words. Then I realized I had to correct what I’d said earlier.
hunks.sol: I stared at Michael Silbert, at a loss for words. Then I realized I needed to correct what I’d said earlier.

hunks.baseline: “……Now that I think about it, you’re not just crazy. You’re completely out of your fucking mind.”
hunks.sol: “……Now that I look at you again, you’re not just a crazy bastard. You’re completely out of your fucking mind.”

hunks.baseline: “Call me whatever you like for now. By the time the sun sets, everything will be decided. Whether you and your friends live or die, and the name the world will know as my true one.”
hunks.sol: “Call me whatever you like for now. By the time the sun sets, everything will be decided. Whether you and those friends of yours live or die, and the name the world will know as my true one.”

hunks.baseline: But the “true name” he’d just mentioned meant something else.
hunks.sol: But that wasn’t what he meant by his “true name.”

hunks.baseline: Depending on how this fight turned out, he might become the Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation—or become a new Demon King.
hunks.sol: Depending on how this fight turned out, he could become the Alliance Leader of the World Hunter Federation—or the new Demon King.

hunks.baseline: Of course, to me, that was just something Michael Silbert had decided for himself.
hunks.sol: Of course, as far as I was concerned, that was all in Michael Silbert’s head.

hunks.baseline: His face slowly stiffened. I let out a scornful laugh.
hunks.sol: His face slowly stiffened. I couldn’t help laughing.

hunks.baseline: “An imugi that lives in a clear pond ascends to heaven. Ever seen a grub wriggling in a sewer turn into a dragon? No matter how strong you get, your nature stays the same. At best, you’re a mosquito or a leech.”
hunks.sol: “An imugi from a clear pond ascends to heaven. Ever seen a grub wriggling in a sewer turn into a dragon? No matter how strong you get, your nature stays the same. At best, you’re a mosquito or a leech.”

hunks.baseline: “A mosquito drunk on power, with its straw stuck in a Magic Gem. A useless leech that does nothing but suck people’s blood. That’s what you are, you pathetic bastard.”
hunks.sol: “A mosquito drunk on power, with a straw stuck in a Magic Gem. A useless leech that does nothing but suck people’s blood. That’s what you are, you pathetic bastard.”

hunks.baseline: If the end of that laughable ambition of his was just taking control of the World Hunter Federation, if his only goal was to stand at the top… then maybe no more disasters would happen.
hunks.sol: If the end of his pathetic ambition was simply taking control of the World Hunter Federation, if his only goal was to stand at the top… I’d thought maybe no more disasters would happen.

hunks.baseline: I was in pain.
hunks.sol: It hurt.

hunks.baseline: I had power and abilities that everyone wanted, yet I couldn’t save the cities crumbling into ruins or the countless people dying inside them.
hunks.sol: I had the power and abilities everyone wished for, yet I couldn’t save the cities collapsing into ruins or the countless people dying inside them.

hunks.baseline: It felt as if I were the one causing this terrible disaster by standing against Michael Silbert.
hunks.sol: It felt as though these terrible disasters were happening because I’d stood against Michael Silbert.

hunks.baseline: That was why, for a little while, I couldn’t help but wonder.
hunks.sol: For a while, I couldn’t help wondering if I should stop.

hunks.baseline: I was afraid to keep running along this path, paved with countless deaths.
hunks.sol: I was afraid to keep running down a path strewn with countless dead.

hunks.baseline: The closer I chased Michael Silbert, the more blood and bodies I feared I’d trample underfoot.
hunks.sol: The longer I chased Michael Silbert, the more blood and bodies I feared I’d find beneath my feet.

hunks.baseline: When I finally came out of the dark, endless tunnel I’d walked alone inside my heart, where no one else could see, there was the light I’d wanted so badly.
hunks.sol: When I finally came out of that long, dark tunnel I’d walked alone in my heart, where no one else could see, there was the light I’d wanted so badly.

hunks.baseline: All of it had come from my own weakness. My foolish hope was wrong, and Michael Silbert was a monster who wouldn’t stop running even after he crossed the finish line.
hunks.sol: That hope had been born of my own weakness. Michael Silbert was a monster who wouldn’t stop running even after he crossed the finish line.

hunks.baseline: That was why I had to kill him as a human being.
hunks.sol: That was why I had to kill him, as a human being.

hunks.baseline: “No matter how I look at it, the answer is still to stomp on leeches like you until they burst. Don’t you think?”
hunks.sol: “No matter how I look at it, the answer is to stomp on leeches like you until they burst. Don’t you think?”

hunks.baseline: His eyes had turned so black there was no trace of their original color. At the same time, an immense, seemingly endless power wrapped around his entire body and began to whirl.
hunks.sol: His eyes had turned so black that no trace of their original color remained. An immense, seemingly endless power swirled around his body.

hunks.baseline: Everything the strands of power touched broke and split apart.
hunks.sol: Everything the rising strands of power touched broke and split apart.

hunks.baseline: His voice, once gentle and unhurried, rang out as if it belonged to something from another world.
hunks.sol: His voice, once gentle and unhurried, rang out as though it belonged to something from another world.

hunks.baseline: The truth, huh?
hunks.sol: *The truth, huh?*

hunks.baseline: I could more or less guess. Why wasn’t Michael Silbert, who loved attention so much, broadcasting the brightest moment of his life to the whole world?
hunks.sol: I had a fair idea why Michael Silbert, who loved attention so much, wasn’t broadcasting the brightest moment of his life to the whole world.

hunks.baseline: But at this moment, there was only one thing I could say to him.
hunks.sol: But right now, there was only one thing I could say to him.

hunks.baseline: As I charged toward his energy, surging like waves across a boundless sea, I suddenly wondered why that immense power—enough to make even my three jiazi of internal energy feel hopelessly inadequate—didn’t frighten me.
hunks.sol: As I charged toward his surging waves of energy, I suddenly wondered why that immense power—enough to make even my three jiazi of internal energy feel hopelessly inadequate—didn’t frighten me.

hunks.baseline: Why Michael Silbert, who’d absorbed a Magic Gem and gained physical abilities comparable to mine and a seemingly inexhaustible supply of magical power, seemed so small.
hunks.sol: Why Michael Silbert, who’d absorbed a Magic Gem and gained physical abilities comparable to mine and an inexhaustible supply of magical power, seemed so small.

hunks.baseline: And as I thrust out the spearhead, I found the answer.
hunks.sol: As I thrust out the spearhead, I found the answer.
